title: Should tourists pay more to visit?

turns.speaker: Yasmin
turns.text: Venice charges day visitors now, and three other cities have announced something similar since.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: Five euros isn't going to deter anyone who flew there. It's a gesture.

turns.speaker: Greta
turns.text: It's a gesture that raises money, mind you. And the stated aim was never really deterrence, it was funding the cleaning and the crowd management.

turns.speaker: Yasmin
turns.text: Although day visitors are the ones who spend least and cost most, so charging them specifically makes sense.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: The cruise passenger who eats on the ship and uses the square for four hours.

turns.speaker: Greta
turns.text: Exactly that. The economics of a cruise call are genuinely bad for a small city.

turns.speaker: Yasmin
turns.text: The deeper problem is housing, though, and a day charge does nothing about it.

turns.speaker: Greta
turns.text: Short-term lets, yes. That's what actually empties a centre of residents, and it's a separate policy entirely.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: Barcelona went at that directly rather than charging visitors. Phasing out tourist flat licences altogether.

turns.speaker: Yasmin
turns.text: Which is far more aggressive and much more likely to work.

turns.speaker: Greta
turns.text: There's an equity objection worth taking seriously, though. A charge prices out the backpacker and not the cruise line.

turns.speaker: Paolo
turns.text: So charge per visit but scale it to what the visit costs the city.

turns.speaker: Yasmin
turns.text: Which would land hardest on cruises, and that is exactly why it won't happen.

points: Venice and other cities have introduced charges for day visitors.
Paolo argues small charges do not deter anyone; Greta notes the aim is funding cleaning and crowd management rather than deterrence.
Day visitors, particularly cruise passengers, spend least while imposing the highest costs.
Yasmin argues the deeper problem is housing, which visitor charges do not address.
Barcelona instead targeted short-term lets by phasing out tourist flat licences, which they consider more effective.
Greta raises an equity objection, since flat charges affect budget travellers more than cruise lines, and Yasmin notes cost-based charging is unlikely for that reason.
